arxiv-2010-16198.title: Automatic Myocardial Infarction Evaluation from Delayed-Enhancement Cardiac MRI using Deep Convolutional Networks
arxiv-2010-16198.creator: Kibrom Berihu Girum, Youssef Skandarani, Raabid Hussain, Alexis Bozorg Grayeli, Gilles Créhange, Alain Lalande
arxiv-2010-16198.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a new deep learning framework for an automatic myocardial infarction evaluation from clinical information and delayed enhancement-MRI (DE-MRI). The proposed framework addresses two tasks. The first task is automatic detection of myocardial contours, the infarcted area, the no-reflow area, and the left ventricular cavity from a short-axis DE-MRI series.

arxiv-2112-07788.title: CdS/CdSe/CdS spherical quantum wells as single-photon sources
arxiv-2112-07788.creator: A. Allemand, F. Kulzer, B. Mahler, C. Dujardin and J. Houel
arxiv-2112-07788.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by A. Allemand, F. Kulzer, B. Mahler, C. Dujardin and J. Houel. We have synthesized CdS(1.3 nm)/CdSe(1.7 nm)/CdS(3.4 nm) spherical quantum wells with 13 nm diameter and demonstrated the first antibunching of their emission, labelling them as single-photon sources. Antibunching survives even at high excitation intensities, ruling-out any bi-exciton emission. For the largest intensities, antibunching coupled to spectral measurements, reveal the signature of a blue-shifted emission, associated to an irreversible photo-aging effect. We demonstrate a moderate correlation between the main and the blue-shifted emission energy.

arxiv-2202-03421.title: The Effect of Adiabatic Compression on Dark Matter Halos and the Radial Acceleration Relation
arxiv-2202-03421.creator: Pengfei Li, Stacy S. McGaugh, Federico Lelli, Yong Tian, James M. Schombert, Chung-Ming Ko
arxiv-2202-03421.description: Abstract We use a semi-empirical model to investigate the radial acceleration relation (RAR) in a cold dark matter (CDM) framework. Specifically, we build 80 model galaxies covering the same parameter space as the observed galaxies in the SPARC database, assigning them to dark matter halos using abundance matching and halo mass-concentration relations.

arxiv-2303-14829.title: SEM-POS: Grammatically and Semantically Correct Video Captioning
arxiv-2303-14829.creator: Asmar Nadeem, Adrian Hilton, Robert Dawes, Graham Thomas, Armin Mustafa
arxiv-2303-14829.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Asmar Nadeem, Adrian Hilton, Robert Dawes, Graham Thomas, Armin Mustafa. Generating grammatically and semantically correct captions in video captioning is a challenging task. The captions generated from the existing methods are either word-by-word that do not align with grammatical structure or miss key information from the input videos. To address these issues, we introduce a novel global-local fusion network, with a Global-Local Fusion Block (GLFB) that encodes and fuses features from different parts of speech (POS) components with visual-spatial features.

arxiv-2402-16128.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Sandeep Singh, Ramandeep Kaur. For integers m m and n n , the Baumslag-Solitar groups, denoted as B ​ S ​ ( m , n ) BS(m,n) , are groups generated by two elements with a single defining relation: B S ( m , n ) = ⟨ a , b | a m b = b a n ⟩ BS(m,n)=\langle a,b|a^{m}b=ba^{n}\rangle .

arxiv-2402-19323.title: Fault-tolerant structures for measurement-based quantum computation on a network
arxiv-2402-19323.creator: Yves van Montfort, Sébastian de Bone, David Elkouss
arxiv-2402-19323.description: Abstract In this work, we introduce a method to construct fault-tolerant measurement-based quantum computation (MBQC) architectures and numerically estimate their performance over various types of networks. A possible application of such a paradigm is distributed quantum computation, where separate computing nodes work together on a fault-tolerant computation through entanglement.

arxiv-2405-20715.title: Transforming Japan Real Estate
arxiv-2405-20715.creator: Diab Haque
arxiv-2405-20715.description: Abstract The Japanese commercial and residential real estate markets, with a combined estimated value surpassing 35 trillion US dollars, present a significant opportunity for investors. Accurate forecasting of rents and prices could provide a substantial competitive edge in this market.

arxiv-2408-06981.title: A Drinfeld type presentation of twisted Yangians of quasi-split type
arxiv-2408-06981.creator: Kang Lu, Weinan Zhang
arxiv-2408-06981.description: Abstract . We formulate a family of algebras, twisted Yangians (of simply-laced quasi-split type) in Drinfeld type current generators and defining relations. These new algebras admit PBW type bases and are shown to be a deformation of twisted current algebras.

arxiv-2501-06044.title: Beyond Optimal Fault-Tolerance
arxiv-2501-06044.creator: Andrew Lewis-Pye, Tim Roughgarden
arxiv-2501-06044.description: Abstract . One of the most basic properties of a consensus protocol is its fault-tolerance—the maximum fraction of faulty participants that the protocol can tolerate without losing fundamental guarantees such as safety and liveness. Because of its importance, the optimal fault-tolerance achievable by any protocol has been characterized in a wide range of settings.

arxiv-2505-09236.title: Approximate Cartesian Tree Matching with One Difference Note: A previous version of this paper was presented at the 30th edition of the Symposium on String Processing and Information Retrieval (SPIRE 2023).
arxiv-2505-09236.creator: Bastien Auvray, Julien David, Samah Ghazawi, Richard Groult, Gad M. Landau, Thierry Lecroq
arxiv-2505-09236.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Bastien Auvray, Julien David, Samah Ghazawi, Richard Groult, Gad M. Landau, Thierry Lecroq. Cartesian tree pattern matching consists of finding all the factors of a text that have the same Cartesian tree than a given pattern. There already exist theoretical and practical solutions for the exact case. In this paper, we propose the first algorithms for solving approximate Cartesian tree pattern matching with one difference given a pattern of length m m and a text of length n n .

arxiv-2506-12266.title: The Behavior Gap: Evaluating Zero-shot LLM Agents in Complex Task-Oriented Dialogs
arxiv-2506-12266.creator: Avinash Baidya, Kamalika Das, Xiang Gao
arxiv-2506-12266.description: Abstract Large Language Model (LLM)-based agents have significantly impacted Task-Oriented Dialog Systems (TODS) but continue to face notable performance challenges, especially in zero-shot scenarios. While prior work has noted this performance gap, the behavioral factors driving the performance gap remain under-explored.

pmc-10501169.title: Advances in smart delivery of magnetic field-targeted drugs in cardiovascular diseases
pmc-10501169.creator: Xinyu Wang, Ruru Bai
pmc-10501169.description: Magnetic Drug Targeting (MDT) is of particular interest to researchers because of its good loading efficiency, targeting accuracy, and versatile use in vivo. Cardiovascular Disease (CVD) is a global chronic disease with a high mortality rate, and the development of more precise and effective treatments is imminent.

pmc-11322129.title: Attachment and propensity for reporting compassionate opportunities and behavior in everyday life
pmc-11322129.creator: Deanna Varley, Chase S. Sherwell, James N. Kirby
pmc-11322129.description: IntroductionResearchers have identified links between anxious and avoidant attachments and difficulties with self-compassion, giving others compassion, and receiving compassion. However, while compassion requires both awareness of opportunities for compassion and compassionate action, little is known about attachment-related differences in reporting compassionate opportunities. Further, most research relies on retrospective-reports that may not accurately assess compassionate behaviors in everyday life.

pmc-11435689.title: Application of Indoor Positioning Systems in Nursing Homes: Enhancing Resident Safety and Staff Efficiency
pmc-11435689.creator: Chia-Rong Lee, Edward T-H Chu, Min-Jing Sie, Li-Tsai Lin, Mei-Zhen Hong, Ching-Chih Huang, Frank Deinzer
pmc-11435689.description: Providing a safe and secure living environment for residents that is supported by a dedicated healthcare team is one of the core values of nursing homes. Nursing homes must protect residents from the risk of going missing, track quarantined residents and visitors to control the spread of infection, and maintain proactive nursing rounds.

pmc-11438163.title: How to enhance MSCs therapeutic properties? An insight on potentiation methods
pmc-11438163.creator: Cynthia Aylín García-Guerrero, Paloma Fuentes, María Jesús Araya, Farida Djouad, Patricia Luz-Crawford, Ana María Vega-Letter, Claudia Altamirano
pmc-11438163.description: Mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (MSCs) have emerged as a promising tool in the field of regenerative medicine due to their unique therapeutic properties as they can differentiate into multiple cell types and exert paracrine effects. However, despite encouraging results obtained in preclinical studies, clinical trials have not achieved the same levels of efficacy.

pmc-11546059.title: Assessment of Professional Practices in the Care Pathway of Patients with Upper Aerodigestive Tract Cancer in a University Hospital
pmc-11546059.creator: Dounia Chbihi, Morgane Corda, Thomas Thibault, Jérémy Baude, Caroline Guigou, Mireille Folia
pmc-11546059.description: Objectives: The main objective of this study was to evaluate the alignment between treatment decisions made during multidisciplinary team meetings (MTMs) and the treatments received by patients with upper aerodigestive tract cancers. The secondary objective was to identify factors influencing potential discrepancies.

pmc-11812516.title: Patient education tools for chronic pain medications, AI versus traditional PILs – Clarifications
pmc-11812516.creator: Prakash Gondode, Sakshi Duggal, Neha Garg, Surendar Sethupathy, Omshubham Asai, Pooja Lohakare
pmc-11812516.description: traditional patient information leaflets (PILs), setting a foundation for future research on patient engagement.[4] We addressed expert panel bias with a diverse team, using objective tools like readability scores and Patient Education Material Assessment Tool (PEMAT) to complement subjective evaluations.

pmc-12460172.title: Conditional generation of real antigen-specific T cell receptor sequences
pmc-12460172.creator: Dhuvarakesh Karthikeyan, Sarah N Bennett, Amy G Reynolds, Benjamin G Vincent, Alex Rubinsteyn
pmc-12460172.description: Despite recent advances in T cell receptor (TCR) engineering, designing functional TCRs against arbitrary targets remains challenging due to complex rules governing cross-reactivity and limited paired data. Here we present TCR-TRANSLATE, a sequence-to-sequence framework that adapts low-resource machine translation techniques to generate antigen-specific TCR sequences against unseen epitopes.

pmc-12558734.title: Ménière’s disease and vestibular migraine: a narrative review of pathogenetic insights, diagnostic evolution, and clinical management advances
pmc-12558734.creator: Hongwei Sun, Gang Zhang, Yingxin Zhang, Tong Li, Xiuzhen Du, Zhensheng Fang
pmc-12558734.description: Ménière’s disease (MD) and vestibular migraine (VM) are two common vestibular disorders with significant clinical overlap in their symptomatic presentations, including vertigo, hearing loss, tinnitus, and aural fullness. Although distinct diagnostic criteria exist for each, this symptomatic similarity often makes early-stage differentiation challenging.

pmc-12619178.title: Multivariate analysis of determinants and development of a predictive algorithm for successful labor induction in nulliparous women
pmc-12619178.creator: Neifang Wei, Zhiyun Wang
pmc-12619178.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe present investigation aims to develop an innovative predictive nomogram capable of predicting successful labor induction in nulliparous women, thereby elucidating critical determinants influencing such success and estimating the probability of successful induction in term singleton pregnancies.MethodsThis retrospective cohort analysis included 1,000 term pregnant nulliparas who underwent labor induction in the Ultrasound Department of the National Traditional Chinese Medicine Hospital in Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture between January 2017 and December 2024.

pmc-13434554.title: ‘It’s a healthy choice’: a qualitative study of Australian consumers’ awareness and interpretation of nutrition-related claims on alcohol products
pmc-13434554.creator: Asad Yusoff, Alexandra Jones, Bella Sträuli, Paula O’Brien, Jacqueline Bowden, Simone Pettigrew
pmc-13434554.description: Objectives:Alcohol companies are increasingly marketing products with nutrition-related claims to appeal to consumers. There are concerns around the potential of such claims to mislead; however, there is limited research on consumers’ attitudes to claims, why they use them and how they influence product selection. The aim of this study was to explore these issues among Australian consumers.
